page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.8xlarge is a shared-core compute instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz using the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX and AVX-512 extensions alongside AES encryption primitives. The instance has no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and includes no GPUs. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate marked divergence between single-threaded and parallel execution profiles. Single-threaded metrics, including the Geekbench single-core score of 904.0 and stress-ng single-core throughput of 1022.19, rank in the bottom 10 percent of evaluated instances. Similar constraints appear in single-threaded compression tests, where gzip achieves 19.03 GB/sec. When leveraged across all available cores, the system reaches average-tier performance, producing a PassMark CPU score of 25,113.13 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 8,644.0. Text processing performance remains weak, while large-block read-only memory bandwidth registers at 81.51 GB/sec.

The shared CPU allocation model and lower RAM-to-CPU ratio provide a cost-efficient footprint for scale-out parallel workloads that can tolerate variable thread availability. However, the shared tenancy model and modest single-core throughput introduce performance tradeoffs for latency-sensitive or clock-dependent tasks. With 27.29 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and static web serving capacity of 18.55 GB/sec, the instance is appropriate for horizontal web serving, non-critical batch processing, parallel compilation, and secondary CI/CD worker nodes.

The system provides 64.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero local storage, and no GPU hardware. Benchmark results display poor single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 904.0, but stabilize within average percentiles under multi-core loads, such as a PassMark CPU score of 25,113.13 and multi-threaded decompression rates of 95.32 GB/sec.
